inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (1,859M; cover page 1,852.5M basic at 2026-07-17). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and buybacks (FY2025 $1,396M; H1-2026 $518M) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat. No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 = $54M (10-K). Equity-award withholding tax not separately tagged; immaterial at <0.4% of revenue. Interest income not stripped: CSX is a net-debt company (net debt ~$17.5B).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity = 4.3% 10y UST + 0.95 beta x 4.75% ERP = ~8.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% x (1-0.24) = 3.0%; market weights ~82% equity / 18% debt (mkt cap ~$87B, debt $18.9B) -> WACC ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality, coal exposure and the UP-NS competitive threat are charged in the bear/bull flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (liability $546M at FY2025) are already expensed inside operating expense and hence EBITDA; lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (one treatment, charged once in the flows). Finance leases are inside LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations and remain in debt.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $18,864M = long-term debt and finance leases $17,162M + current portion $1,702M (Q2 2026 10-Q). Cash $1,390M = cash, equivalents and restricted cash $1,007M + short-term investments $383M. Net debt $17,474M at 2026-06-30.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: operating company, cyclical US industrial). CSX is a Class I freight railroad (~20,000 route miles, eastern US) -- a capital-intensive quasi-infrastructure operator whose value is its free cash flow after maintenance/growth capex; none of the non-FCF rows apply. Adaptations applied: cyclical (risk charged once, in flows/weights), lease treatment stated. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $14,092M, EBITDA $6,201M = 44.0%, depressed by Hurricane Helene Blue Ridge rebuild, Howard Street Tunnel detours, weak coal/merchandise pricing and Q3-Q4 2025 restructuring). FY2025 reported FCF $1,711M is a TROUGH: capex $2,902M (20.6% of revenue) was elevated by the Blue Ridge and Howard Street projects; TTM to Q2 2026 capex is $2,526M (17.4%) and H1-2026 $1,119M (15.1%). last_fcf ($1,657M) is recorded for audit only -- the forward flows are built from components on unlevered EBIT and do not carry the FY2025 margin forward. H1-2026 EBITDA margin 48.3% (Q2 48.7%) reflects the post-Sept-2025 cost programme under the new CEO. Buybacks funded (repurchaser), so the flat count is paid for in cash. Analysis JSON was not yet available at build time; narratives drawn from filings data and business knowledge.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 10yr CAGR 1.8% and 5yr 5.9% (off the FY2020 COVID base) bracketed; ~3% = nominal GDP-like volume plus inflation-plus pricing
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.1% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (5.9%) and EPS (5.1%) CAGRs. Book value is not a growth measure here: CSX returns essentially all FCF via dividends and buybacks ($4.7B repurchased FY2022), so equity is flat by policy. EPS 5yr CAGR uses FY2020 EPS split-adjusted for the June-2021 3:1 split (3.61/3).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (SBC deducted, no interest-income strip as net debt) track reported FCF closely because SBC is <0.4% of revenue. Both are strongly negative over 3 and 5 years because FY2022 FCF ($3.4B) was a peak (low capex, strong coal pricing) and FY2025 ($1.7B) a trough (hurricane/tunnel capex, weak pricing) -- neither end is a run-rate, which is why the forward build uses components rather than these CAGRs.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +5% (H1-2026 +6% y/y, Q2 +10% off a disrupted Q2-2025), then GDP-plus 3-3.5% fading to 2.5%. EBITDA margin holds the H1-2026 cost-programme gains at ~48% (vs 44% FY2025, 47.5% FY2024, 50% FY2022). Capex normalises from 20.6% to 15.5% of revenue as Blue Ridge and Howard Street complete -- still above D&A (11%) because track and rolling stock replace at inflated prices.
base.capex_note: Long-run 15.5% vs FY2019-2022 average ~15%; FY2023-25 17-21% included project spend.

scenario_narratives.base: CSX consolidates the 2026 operating recovery: the Blue Ridge (Helene) line and the Howard Street Tunnel double-stack clearance are finished, the post-2025 management change's cost programme holds EBITDA margin near 48%, and volumes grow with the eastern-US industrial economy plus modest intermodal share gains from trucks. Export coal drifts lower and is offset by merchandise pricing above rail inflation. The Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern combination (if approved by the STB) competes for some eastern single-line traffic but CSX keeps its franchise via interline partnerships (BNSF). Capex settles at ~15.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: Precision-scheduled-railroading discipline returns CSX to peer-leading margins (EBITDA ~51%, operating ratio high-50s), Howard Street double-stack and I-95 corridor reshoring/nearshoring drive intermodal and merchandise growth of 4-5%, and capex intensity falls to ~14.5% once the catch-up projects roll off. Rail-merger consolidation (a BNSF or CPKC combination answering UP-NS) is optionality not modelled in the flows, but the growth path reflects the network gaining single-line reach through partnerships.
scenario_narratives.bear: An industrial/freight recession in 2027 flattens volumes, export and domestic coal (roughly an eighth of revenue) accelerates its decline, and a merged UP-NS transcontinental diverts eastern single-line intermodal and chemicals traffic. Service slips again (as in 2022 and 2025), cost savings leak back and EBITDA margin settles at ~45%; capex stays elevated at 16.5% for resilience (weather hardening, PTC/tech renewal). Terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap reflect a structurally slower franchise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): freight is cyclical, coal is in secular decline and the UP-NS merger is a genuine competitive shock the eastern network has not faced since Conrail. Base 50%: H1-2026 margins already show the cost programme working. Bull 30% (down from 35%): it needs volume growth, margin expansion and a capex step-down to all land at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A railroad is durable, hard-to-replicate infrastructure with pricing power, but it is also a heavy reinvester: capex has run 15-21% of revenue against D&A of ~11%, so owner FCF is materially below net income plus depreciation. The model values the unlevered owner FCF from a component build (EBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> 24% cash tax on EBIT -> capex -> working capital) at an 8% USD WACC, deducts $17.5B net debt at the June 2026 balance sheet, and divides by a flat 1,859M diluted shares.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity: each 1pp of revenue in perpetual capex is ~$150M/yr of FCF, roughly $1.4/share
Margin durability of the 2026 cost programme after the 2025 CEO change
UP-NS merger approval and its traffic diversion from eastern single-line competition
Export coal price/volume (thermal and met) and industrial cycle
Terminal value share is high for a low-growth, long-duration asset; the market price embeds a lower discount rate than 8%
